query: evidence that older methods for For each synchronized detection and depth pair, send stage 2 only the pallet select_detection already chooses, and write both sides of that split onto the result the handling process reads. PalletPoseStamped gains the chosen candidate's source index as the pallet sent through stage 2, and the source indices of the other class-matched candidates in that same Detection2DArray as deferred. Those indices are the slots extract_detection_candidates already stored. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the roster is this capture while the scene can still change. When the estimate fails, the same two lists go on the failure diagnostic, which is the only result that path publishes. The two early returns that publish nothing stay as they are. Stage 2 still runs once. The user named which detections are sent versus deferred; the part they did not name is that both lists sit on PalletPoseStamped, the pose result for the AGV controller, rather than only on a diagnostic the success path does not use. have been superseded
findings: Registering the whole scene cloud down to one pallet, and naming no other pallet, is the older front end. Shao, Fan, Zhu, Lu, and Lang, Sensors 2023, 23(3):1217, say existing pose methods miss real-time accuracy because the scene cloud is enormous. They pass-through filter, voxel-downsample, plane-segment a single target cloud, and register it with AGWF-FPFH, SAC-IA, and ICP. Against FPFH and SHOT, that change is a faster descriptor on the same registration: more than 30% off feature-extraction time and more than 35% accuracy. The result is one rigid transform. Isaac ROS FoundationPose 5.0 builds the stage-2 mask from only the highest-scoring detection in the Detection2DArray and publishes a vision_msgs/Detection3DArray pose. Lang2Lift, Nguyen et al., arXiv:2508.15427, outputs one top-1 mask per prompt and runs FoundationPose on that mask, then couples that pose to forklift planning and control in a cluttered outdoor scene. Those later pipelines supersede whole-scene registration as the way to choose the pallet stage 2 sees. They still do not write the other detections' source indices onto the pose the controller reads.

A 6D pose for every detected pallet has not been superseded. Wu and Demeester, VISIGRAPP 2026, pass pixels inside each detector bounding box into FoundationPose, and the pose selection module writes a 6D pose for each pallet bin. Their second-stage choice ranks rotation hypotheses of that bin. On their hardware, RF-DETR-S takes about 21 ms and FoundationPose takes about 2.8 s per frame. Single stage-2, as in Isaac ROS and Lang2Lift, coexists with that full pass.

Keeping the unselected pallets as tracks across later scans, then deleting the weak ones, is the older roster, and a later scan is not this capture. Mohamed, Capitanelli, Mastrogiovanni, Rovetta, and Zaccaria, arXiv:1803.11254, do not immediately accept a pallet. A Kalman filter defers commitment until later scans agree, and a candidate whose average confidence falls below 0.35, or that stays invisible past 0.6 s, is discarded. Meng, Ren, Yu, Yin, Wang, and Men, Sensors 2024, 24(16):5330, say most earlier research positioned a single pallet and ignored stacks. They decide inside the current view: a width-pixel window (WP and WT), a depth window from D-DF to D+DB, unloading priority, with the upper pallet first, and they transform that one target into the forklift frame. sensor_msgs/Image says the header stamp should be the acquisition time of that image. vision_msgs Detection2D says the source pixels are not in the message, the header should match the source, and the consumer recovers that source with an exact or approximate synchronizer. Detection2D.id may be empty and is an id meant to stay the same across messages, not the slot in this Detection2DArray. Meng's other pallets are already in the same view, and Lang2Lift's pick is in a cluttered outdoor scene, so a later frame is not a stand-in for the indices this pair already stored. Meng still does not put those other indices on the pose.

Throwing away every detection below a score threshold, and keeping no identity for it, is the older bookkeeping ByteTrack superseded for tracking, and that replacement still does not land on the pose. Zhang et al., ByteTrack, ECCV 2022, say trackers that keep only boxes above a threshold throw away true objects and fragment trajectories. BYTE keeps almost every box, splits a high-score set from a low-score set, and associates the low-score set with tracks the first pass left unmatched. Unmatched low-score boxes are deleted as background. The per-frame output is track boxes and identities, not the chosen source index and the other class-matched indices on a pose result.

Leaving the unselected indices only on a diagnostic the success path does not read has been separated from the result a controller consumes, and no fetched source has superseded that placement by putting both lists on the pose. geometry_msgs/PoseStamped is still a header and a pose. The ROS diagnostics README says the system collects hardware state for users and operators; the flow is /diagnostics to an aggregator, rqt_runtime_monitor, rqt_robot_monitor, and remote logging. DiagnosticArray is diagnostic information about the state of the robot. DiagnosticStatus carries a level, OK, WARN, ERROR, or STALE, plus KeyValue pairs, not detection-array slots. The ros2_control hardware_status draft says free-form key/value diagnostics are for logs, dashboards, and human inspection, ideally not parsed by control loops, while structured status is what controllers read. That draft is not a released message, and it does not carry a sent index and a deferred index list. Isaac ROS publishes Detection3DArray. Lang2Lift couples the one pose to planning and control. Meng publishes the one target in the forklift frame. None of them put this capture's other class-matched source indices on that pose. When the estimate fails, the same gap remains: a failure DiagnosticArray is still the operator status stream unless the handling process is the subscriber of that status, and the draft does not move a failed pose's roster onto the pose result.
